groups.title: Antihistamine Decongestant Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion and watery eyes caused by a head cold and by allergic or vasomotor rhinitis.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 tablet per dose; for children aged 12 to 14 years, 1/2 tablet per dose, 3 times a day after meals.
groups.caution: If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine or to methyl parahydroxybenzoate. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion and watery eyes from a cold or rhinitis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Hypersensitivity to this medicine or preservatives; serious skin reactions

groups.title: Expectorant Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for difficulty bringing up phlegm in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis.
groups.usage: For acute disease, adults take 1 capsule (200 mg) 3 times a day and children aged 6 to 14 years take 1 capsule (200 mg) 2 times a day. For chronic disease, adults take 1 capsule (200 mg) 2 times a day and children aged 6 to 14 years take 1/2 capsule (100 mg) 3 times a day. For cystic fibrosis, children aged 6 years and over take 1 capsule (200 mg) 3 times a day. Take before meals with a small amount of water.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, have a gastric or duodenal ulcer, are an infant under 2 years, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Difficulty bringing up phlegm in bronchitis, asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 2 years; gastric or duodenal ulcer; galactose intolerance

groups.title: Antihistamine Decongestant Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion and watery eyes caused by a head cold and by allergic or vasomotor rhinitis.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 tablet per dose; for children aged 12 to 14 years, 1/2 tablet per dose, 3 times a day after each meal.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, have severe hepatic or renal impairment, severe heart disease, difficulty passing urine with residual urine, high blood pressure or coronary artery disease, or are receiving an MAO inhibitor. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion and watery eyes from a cold or rhinitis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: MAO inhibitor use; hypertension, heart disease, urinary difficulty

groups.title: Cold Relief Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 2 tablets 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions have been reported; stop taking it immediately if a rash or other sign of hypersensitivity appears.

summaryTable.Use: Cold symptoms: sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, aches
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 15 years; regular alcohol use; serious skin reactions

groups.title: Mucolytic Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used as a mucolytic and expectorant in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 capsule (300 mg) 2 to 3 times a day. For acute respiratory disease, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, or have liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer or severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance < 25 mL/min). Before taking it, patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Mucolytic and expectorant in acute and chronic respiratory disease

groups.title: Antidiarrhoeal Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for diarrhoea, diarrhoea with abdominal pain, a feeling of heaviness, loose stools and vomiting with diarrhoea.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 2 tablets 3 times a day after meals. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, are a newborn or a child aged 7 years or under, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Digestive Enzyme Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for indigestion, loss of appetite, overeating, a feeling of heaviness, promotion of digestion, and a feeling of fullness in the stomach caused by indigestion.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over, 1 to 2 tablets 3 times a day after meals. For people aged 8 years to under 15 years, 1 tablet 3 times a day after meals.
groups.caution: Do not give to children aged 7 years or under. Before taking it, people with an allergic constitution, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, and people hypersensitive to Yellow No. 4 should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Indigestion, loss of appetite, overeating, stomach fullness
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 7 years or under; pregnancy; tartrazine sensitivity

groups.title: Vitamin D Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used as supportive treatment for osteoporosis, and to prevent the risk of vitamin D deficiency disease and to prevent rickets in healthy people without malabsorption.
groups.usage: As supportive treatment for osteoporosis, take 1 tablet (1000 IU) once a day. To prevent the risk of vitamin D deficiency disease and to prevent rickets, take 1/2 tablet (500 IU) once a day. Adults take it with plenty of water. For young children who find the tablet hard to swallow, place the tablet on a spoon, let it disintegrate in water and give it with a meal where possible. When adding it to food, add it after the food has been boiled, and the dose may need adjusting if the food is rich in vitamin D.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, have high blood calcium, high urine calcium or kidney stones, are an infant under 3 months, or have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or a related genetic problem. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Supportive treatment for osteoporosis; prevention of vitamin D deficiency and rickets
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 3 months; high blood or urine calcium; kidney stones

groups.title: Vitamin B1 Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to improve physical fatigue, as a tonic, and to supply vitamin B1 during and after illness.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 1 capsule 2 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine. Keep to the stated directions and amount. If there is no improvement after about 1 month, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Physical fatigue; tonic; vitamin B1 supply during and after illness
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Hypersensitivity; no improvement after 1 month

groups.title: Acetaminophen Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, period pain, sprain pain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: For children aged 12 years and over and adults, 1 to 2 tablets 3 to 4 times a day (every 4 to 6 hours) as needed. Do not exceed 4 g (8 tablets) a day. Take the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions have been reported; stop taking it immediately if a rash or other sign of hypersensitivity appears.

summaryTable.Use: Fever and pain from a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle and joint pain
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 12 years; maximum 4 g a day; regular alcohol use

groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief in headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, low back pain, muscle pain, shoulder pain, bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, period pain and pain from injury, and to reduce fever with chills.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 sachet per dose, up to 3 times a day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions have been reported; stop taking it immediately if a rash or other sign of hypersensitivity appears.

summaryTable.Use: Headache, toothache, sore throat, joint and muscle pain; fever with chills

groups.title: Combined Oral Contraceptive Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for contraception.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet a day for 21 days in the order shown, then have a 7-day break. It is best to take it at about the same time each day. Menstruation occurs during the 7-day break and usually starts 2 to 3 days after the last tablet. If you continue with this medicine, start a new pack after the 7-day break; menstruation may not have finished before the new pack is started. Refer to the detailed approved product information.
groups.caution: Because the risk of serious cardiovascular events such as thrombosis may increase, women taking an oral contraceptive should refrain from smoking. Smokers aged 35 years and over must not take this medicine. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Contraception
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Smoking at 35 years and over; thrombosis risk

groups.title: Calcium Antacid Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for the antacid action and symptom relief of gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, and for calcium supplementation.
groups.usage: For gastric or duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, 2 to 10 tablets (1 to 5 g) a day in 3 to 4 divided doses; for calcium supplementation, 3 to 6 tablets (1.5 to 3 g) a day in 1 to 2 divided doses. Adjust appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution: Do not exceed a maximum of 15 tablets (7.5 g) a day. Do not take if you have severe high blood calcium or severe high urine calcium, hyperparathyroidism or hypothyroidism, severe renal failure, or achlorhydria or gastric acid deficiency. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Antacid for ulcer, gastritis and excess acid; calcium supplementation
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Maximum 15 tablets a day; high blood calcium; renal failure

groups.title: Anti-nausea Oral Liquid
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve nausea and vomiting.
groups.usage: Adults and adolescents (aged 12 years and over, weighing 35 kg and over) take 10 mg (5 mg when receiving levodopa) 3 times a day before meals. The maximum daily amount is 30 mg, and it should generally not be used for more than 1 week.
groups.caution: Do not take if you are hypersensitive to this medicine, if stimulating gastric motility is hazardous (gastrointestinal bleeding, mechanical obstruction, perforation), if you have a prolactin-secreting tumour, if you are receiving a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, or if you have moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Nausea and vomiting
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 12 years or under 35 kg; gastrointestinal bleeding or obstruction; use beyond 1 week

groups.title: Intestinal Adsorbent Powder
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for acute and chronic enteritis, acute and chronic diarrhoea, acute dysentery, and abnormal intestinal fermentation of various causes.
groups.usage: For adults, 2 g 3 times a day, with 4 g for the first dose. For young children, 1 g 3 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not take if you have galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or a genetic problem such as glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Enteritis, diarrhoea, dysentery, abnormal intestinal fermentation
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Galactose intolerance and related genetic problems

groups.title: Acetaminophen Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, period pain, sprain pain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: For adults, 300 to 1000 mg 3 to 4 times a day. Up to 8 tablets (4000 mg) may be taken in a day. It may be adjusted appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions have been reported; stop taking it immediately if a rash or other sign of hypersensitivity appears.

summaryTable.Use: Fever and pain from a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle and joint pain
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Maximum 4000 mg a day; regular alcohol use; serious skin reactions
